problem:
Find ${lim}_{t\to 2}[f(t)+g(t)]$ given that $f(t)$ and $g(t)$ are defined as

$$
\begin{aligned}f(t) & =⟨6-{t}^{3},\,{t}^{2}-6,\,\frac{2}{{t}^{3}}⟩, \\ g(t) & =⟨5-\operatorname{ln}⁡(3-t),\,\sqrt{6-t},\,2t⟩\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.problem:
Find ${lim}_{t\to \,-1}[4f(t)-7g(t)]$ given that $f(t)$ and $g(t)$ are defined as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(t) & ={t}^{3}\,i+{t}^{2}\,j+\operatorname{ln}⁡(t+2)\,k \\ g(t) & =\frac{2}{t}\,i+(3-t)\,j-({t}^{2}-1)k\end{aligned}
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we find the limit of each function:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{t\to \,-1}f(t) & =({lim}_{t\to \,-1}{t}^{3})i+({lim}_{t\to \,-1}{t}^{2})j+({lim}_{t\to \,-1}\operatorname{ln}⁡(t+2))k \\  & =(-1)^{3}\,i+(-1)^{2}\,j+\operatorname{ln}⁡(-1+2)\,k \\  & =-i+j \\ {lim}_{t\to \,-1}g(t) & =({lim}_{t\to \,-1}\frac{2}{t})i+({lim}_{t\to \,-1}(3-t))j-({lim}_{t\to \,-1}({t}^{2}-1))k \\  & =\frac{2}{(-1)}\,i+(3-(-1))\,j-((-1)^{2}-1)k \\  & =-2\,i+4\,j\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we use properties of limits to calculate the final result:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{t\to \,-1}[4f(t)-7g(t)] & ={lim}_{t\to \,-1}4f(t)-{lim}_{t\to \,-1}7g(t) \\  & =4{lim}_{t\to \,-1}f(t)-7{lim}_{t\to \,-1}g(t) \\  & =4(-i+j)-7(-2\,i+4\,j) \\  & =-4\,i+4\,j+14\,i-28\,j \\  & =10\,i-24\,j\end{aligned}
$$
